samples: This program downloads three example websites at the same time, measures how many characters each page body has, and prints the sizes with the largest first. It then fetches two pages from example.com (the home page and a docs page) in parallel under a 10-second deadline and prints their combined size. It needs console and HTTP network access, and it fails if any download fails or the deadline expires. One caution: the last line uses the two results that were bound inside the concurrent block, which may not be visible outside it, so check that it compiles before relying on it.

This program fetches three example web pages in parallel, counts the characters in each body, and prints the sizes from largest to smallest. It then fetches two more pages from example.com (the home page and its docs page) in parallel under a 10-second deadline, and prints their combined character count. It needs console and HTTP access, and it fails if a download fails or the deadline passes. Before relying on it, check that the final line can actually see the two results, because they are created inside the concurrent block and may not be in scope afterward.

This program downloads three example websites in parallel, measures how many characters each page body has, and prints the sites from largest to smallest. It then fetches two more pages (the home page and its docs page) within a 10-second limit and prints their combined size. It needs console and HTTP access, and it fails if a download fails or the time limit expires. One caution: the two values from the last concurrent block are declared inside that block but used after it, which may be a scoping error, so check that it compiles before relying on it.

This program downloads three example websites in parallel, counts the characters in each page body, and prints them with the largest first. It then fetches two pages from the first site under a 10-second deadline and prints their combined size, and the whole run fails if any download fails or the deadline passes. One caution: the final line uses results that were created inside the concurrent block, and if blocks scope their bindings like other Renyi blocks, that line may not compile. It also asks for unrestricted HTTP access instead of limiting it to the sites it uses.

This program fetches the home pages of example.com, example.org and example.net in parallel, then prints each URL with its character count, largest first. It then fetches example.com and example.com/docs under a 10-second deadline and prints their combined size, and it can fail with an HTTP error or a timeout. It needs only console and HTTP access, but the final step reads two results that were bound inside the concurrent block from outside it, which Renyi's scoping rules probably reject, so check that it compiles before relying on it.
